text: Complements, inclusion-exclusion, derangements.

Inclusion-exclusion (容斥原理): to count objects with at least one bad property, add the single properties, subtract the pairs (counted twice), add the triples back, and so on: Σ over non- empty sets S of properties, (−1)|S|+1 · (number having all of S).
Usually you want the objects with no bad property: total − |A ∪ B ∪ …| = Σ over all S (including ∅) of (−1)|S| · N(S).
The art is choosing properties whose intersections are easy to count. Often the simplest form is the complement with a single property.

Prison break (P3197): count rows of n cells, each with one of m religions, where some two neighbours share a religion. Counting "some" directly is messy; its complement "no two neighbours equal" is m·(m − 1)n−1 (the first cell is free, every later one avoids its left neighbour).
Subtract under a modulus with + MOD. n, m reach 10¹², so reduce m before multiplying and use fast power.

A derangement (错排) moves every element. By inclusion-exclusion over "i stays put": D(n) = Σk (−1)k C(n, k)(n − k)!. The same numbers satisfy D(n) = (n − 1)(D(n − 1) + D(n − 2)), which is faster to fill.
Exactly m fixed points (P4071): choose them, C(n, m), and derange the rest: D(n − m). 1, 0, 1, 2, 9, 44 are D(0) … D(5). Inverse factorials are filled backwards from one Fermat inverse (第19章).
Pascal, factorials, models; counting mod k.

Combinations C(n, m) (组合数) count ways to choose m of n items. Three ways to get them: Pascal's rule C(n, m) = C(n−1, m−1) + C(n−1, m) for a whole table up to about 2000 (any modulus, even none); factorials n! / (m!(n−m)!) with inverse factorials for n up to 10⁶ and a prime modulus; Lucas when n is huge and the prime p is small.
Pascal's rule reads: either the last item is chosen (choose m − 1 from the rest) or it is not (choose m from the rest).
This "last item" argument is the start of most counting recurrences.

Combination problem (P2822): for many (n, m), count pairs 0 ≤ j ≤ i ≤ n, j ≤ m with k | C(i, j). C(i, j) is huge, but divisibility by k only needs it mod k, and Pascal's rule works mod anything. Then a 2D prefix sum answers each query in O(1).
For k = 2, n = m = 3 the rows are 1; 1 1; 1 2 1; 1 3 3 1, and only C(2, 1) = 2 is even: answer 1. Store only remainders: the real values overflow long long by row 70.
Query column min(n, m): there are no C(i, j) with j > i, and the prefix sums already count those cells as 0.
Coefficients of (ax + by)^k.

Binomial theorem (二项式定理): (a + b)n = Σk=0..n C(n, k) ak bn−k. Each of the n brackets gives either a or b; choosing which k brackets give a is C(n, k). Setting a = b = 1 gives Σ C(n, k) = 2ⁿ; a = 1, b = −1 gives the alternating sum 0.
Coefficients of polynomials are counting problems in disguise: the coefficient of xk in a product counts ways to pick one term from each factor with exponents adding to k.
Calculate the coefficient (P1313): pick n brackets to give ax and the other m to give by: C(k, n)·aⁿ·bᵐ. (2x + 3y)⁴ has x²y² coefficient C(4, 2)·4·9 = 216.
k ≤ 1000, so Pascal's table is simplest. With k up to 10⁶ switch to factorials and inverse factorials (20.1).
Stack orders; balls into boxes.

Catalan numbers (卡特兰数) 1, 1, 2, 5, 14, 42, … count: push/pop orders of a stack (P1044), balanced bracket strings, binary trees with n nodes, monotone lattice paths that never cross the diagonal, ways to triangulate a polygon. Cat(n) = C(2n, n) / (n + 1) = C(2n, n) − C(2n, n − 1).

Recurrence by the first return: the first element pushed is popped after k others were pushed and popped inside it: Cat(n) = Σk=0..n−1 Cat(k)·Cat(n − 1 − k). The subtraction form comes from reflecting the bad paths at the first crossing.

Stirling numbers of the second kind (第二类斯特林数) S(n, k) count ways to split n distinct items into k non-empty unlabelled groups: the last item either forms its own group, S(n−1, k−1), or joins one of the k groups, k·S(n−1, k). Labelled boxes multiply by k! (P1287 盒子与球).

Catalan under a non-prime modulus (有趣的数列 P3200): factor C(2n, n)/(n + 1) into primes with a sieve, count each prime's exponent, then multiply, avoiding inverses. Staircases (P2532 树屋阶梯) are Catalan numbers with big integers.
